Set the product strategy and multi-cycle roadmap for Search Personalization at Spotify — spanning ranking, relevance, retrieval, AI-native features, quality, and trust.
Drive the evolution of Search toward AI-native experiences — AI Overviews, semantic search, LLM reranking — balancing innovation velocity with quality and cost discipline.
Own the Search quality bar: define how relevance, trust, compliance, and user experience connect into a holistic quality framework with measurable outcomes.
Manage Search’s role as a shared surface across many company strategies — build prioritization frameworks, communicate trade-offs, and represent Search at executive forums.
Influence and coach junior PMs working in Search.
Partner with engineering leadership to make architectural decisions that balance short-term delivery with long-term Search infrastructure health.
Drive cross-functional alignment where Search intersects.

Who You Are

You have 8+ years of product management experience, with 3+ years leading search, discovery, or information retrieval products at scale (100M+ users).
You have a deep technical understanding of search systems — ranking architectures, retrieval strategies, evaluation methodology, and the trade-offs between relevance, latency, cost, and freshness.
You have experience with AI/ML-powered search features — semantic search, LLM-based reranking, recommendations, or similar — and can lead a team through the transition from traditional to AI-native search.
You have a track record of managing complex stakeholder landscapes with competing priorities and limited resources, and can build frameworks for principled prioritization.
You think strategically at the portfolio level — you can synthesize across many concurrent initiatives, set a coherent vision, and communicate it clearly to executives.

You have worked in content integrity, trust & safety, or regulatory compliance in the context of search or discovery systems.

This role is based in London or Stockholm.

About the job

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Technical (External Services), Region Services
jobs.description:
Description

Applicants must be Australian citizens and hold or be eligible to obtain an Australian Government Security Clearance with the ability to successfully complete an Organisational Suitability Assessment. More information regarding security clearances can be found at https://www.agsva.gov.au/.

Based in Melbourne, Sydney or Canberra, we offer relocation support for candidates moving from other states.

The Mission - Why This Program, Why Now?

You're joining at the defining moment of one of the most significant technology programmes Australia has ever undertaken. This programme will build and operate the dedicated cloud giving Australia's national security community and its allies the capability to see more, share more, innovate and act faster than ever before.

The architectural decisions being made now - how we structure services, implement security controls, and automate at scale - will shape how Australia's national security community operates for the next decade. You won't be inheriting someone else's design choices. You'll be making them.

Your Opportunity

Imagine standing at the intersection of strategy, technology, and national purpose, where every product decision you make shapes how an entire AWS cloud region serves Australia's most critical missions. As a Senior Product Manager – Technical, External Services (PMT-ES), you won't just manage a product backlog. You'll own the end-to-end lifecycle of externally-facing AWS services. From defining the technical vision and product strategy, through architecture and launch, to driving adoption and operational excellence with the engineering and IT leaders who depend on your services every day.

This is a role for someone who thrives on complexity, brings deep full-stack technical fluency, and craves impact at scale. You'll define technical requirements alongside engineering teams building the next generation of cloud infrastructure, evaluate architecture trade-offs across performance, scalability, and security, and serve as the voice of the customer for external engineers and IT professionals integrating AWS services into their most critical workloads. When a customer escalation hits, you'll own it, diving deep with engineering to understand the problem, resolve it, and communicate clearly back to technically sophisticated customers.

The Region Services team is redefining how AWS designs, builds, and operates regions. You'll engage directly with technical decision-makers at Australia's most important organisations, understanding how they architect their solutions, generalising requirements across diverse customer personas, and driving service awareness, adoption, and evolution. Your work will directly accelerate Australia's cloud capability and set the standard for how sovereign cloud regions evolve worldwide.

If you're energised by working at the deepest technical levels of cloud services, engaging directly with the engineers and architects who build on AWS, and delivering products that genuinely change how nations operate in the cloud, this is your moment.

Key job responsibilities

Own the end-to-end product lifecycle for externally-facing AWS services in the region, defining service vision, strategy, technical requirements, and roadmaps, while driving capacity planning and service performance.
Define and prioritise product roadmaps by engaging directly with external technical customers (engineers, architects, IT professionals), analysing usage data, service performance metrics, and competitive dynamics to anticipate where customers need to go next.
Partner deeply with engineering teams on architecture decisions, evaluating proposals across performance, scalability, latency, and security trade-offs. Define detailed technical requirements and hold engineering to high standards for service quality.
Serve as the Voice of the Customer distilling requirements from diverse sets of technical customers, understanding how the service integrates into their architectures, and generalising needs across customer personas to define the right product direction.
Own service adoption and operational excellence driving awareness, adoption, and performance optimisation with customers. Own customer escalations, and service communications until issues are resolved.
Collaborate across engineering, design, finance, sales, legal, and operations to align stakeholders, make smart trade-offs, and deliver outcomes that balance customer value with business sustainability.

A day in the life

Your morning begins with a review of service readiness dashboards, tracking which services are on track for launch, where integration testing is surfacing issues, and which customer workload requirements are driving prioritisation decisions. You spot a gap between a customer's architecture needs and a service's planned launch configuration, and pull together the data to make the case for adjusting the rollout sequence.

By mid-morning, you're in a technical design review with the engineering team. A service needs to meet specific compliance requirements before it can go live so you're evaluating the architecture against these constraints, defining the technical requirements, and working through trade-offs between launch timeline and operational readiness.

After lunch, you join a working session with a customer's cloud architects who are planning to migrate mission-critical workloads into the region. They need to understand which services will be available at launch, how they'll perform at scale, and what their migration path looks like. You walk through the region's service roadmap, capture their architectural requirements, and feed those directly into your prioritisation decisions.

The afternoon shifts to a cross-functional alignment session. You're bringing together engineering, capacity planning, compliance, and business development to resolve competing priorities for the launch window. You present your readiness assessment backed by customer commitment data and technical dependency analysis, and drive the group to a decision on what ships in the initial launch versus the fast-follow roadmap.

You end the day knowing that the region you're building will directly enable Australia's national security community to operate with confidence in the cloud and that tomorrow will bring an entirely new set of technical challenges worthy of your expertise.

About The Team

The Region Services team redefines the way AWS designs, builds, and operates AWS regions to enable new cloud infrastructure and services offerings to customers across every industry and of every size, including startups, enterprises, and public sector organisations.

Amazon values inclusive experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. new_jobs.description:

Job Category

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Senior Director, PM - AI Agent Systems

AI agents can reason about what needs to happen. Getting them to reliably do work inside the software businesses actually run on is the next frontier.

We’re building Systems Integration Agent: computer use for the enterprise. It learns how to operate applications like SAP, Oracle, and Workday, then turns that knowledge into reusable, code-backed actions. The challenge goes beyond making an impressive demo: customers need automation they can trust with consequential business processes.

Our team operates as a small startup within Salesforce AI Labs, separate from the main engineering and product organizations. You’ll work directly with the team’s leader and engineers, alongside customers, with the autonomy to shape an early product and the resources of Salesforce to back you up.

As Senior Director of Product Management, you’ll help turn early production success into a repeatable product business. This is a hands-on product leadership role that includes spending time with customers, making difficult prioritization decisions, shaping the experience, and carrying those decisions through launch and adoption. You should be as comfortable investigating a failed customer workflow as presenting the product strategy to executive leadership.

What You’ll Actually Be Doing

Build Directly With Customers

Work alongside enterprise customers to understand their processes, identify valuable automation opportunities, and define what successful execution actually means.
Partner with engineering and forward-deployed engineers to take workflows from initial exploration through production adoption.
Distinguish customer-specific requirements from recurring needs that deserve investment in the core product.
Establish credible measures of customer value, including time saved, operational cost, reliability, and ongoing maintenance.

Own Product Strategy and Prioritization

Shape the product vision, roadmap, and sequencing across agent learning, execution, evaluation, governance, and self-service.
Decide where to focus first: which customers, systems, and workflows offer the strongest combination of customer value and repeatable adoption.
Make explicit tradeoffs between winning a new customer and building capabilities that make the next ten deployments easier.
Translate customer requirements and technical constraints into clear product decisions.

Make Powerful Technology Usable and Trustworthy

Partner with engineering and design to make recording, building, testing, debugging, and operating workflows accessible to the people who own those processes.
Define how users understand what an agent can do, verify its results, recover from failures, and retain control over consequential actions.
Establish product-level success criteria and release gates grounded in task completion, correctness, intervention rates, and time to value.
Build a path from hands-on onboarding toward increasingly self-service adoption.

Take the Product to Market

Partner with Salesforce stakeholders across product marketing, sales, pricing, security, and legal to bring the offering to market.
Shape positioning, packaging, and the customer journey from first demonstration to evaluation, purchase, and production use.
Build a growth strategy that connects enterprise buying decisions with hands-on technical validation and practitioner credibility.
Keep leadership aligned on the investment needed, the evidence behind the strategy, and the decisions that will determine what happens next.

You’re Our Person If…

You’ve taken an enterprise software product from ambiguity into production adoption. You can explain the decisions you owned, what customers actually used, and how the product changed after launch.
You have hands-on experience bringing AI-powered products to users. You understand why model quality alone is insufficient and can reason about evaluation, reliability, latency, cost, and human oversight.
You are technically fluent. You can engage deeply with engineers on agent behavior, APIs, workflow state, permissions, and failure recovery without needing to be the implementation owner.
You build directly with customers. You can move between a CIO’s business objectives and a process owner’s daily work, turning both into focused product decisions.
You demonstrate senior product judgment. You’ve owned consequential roadmap and investment tradeoffs, aligned teams without relying on reporting lines, and stayed accountable for outcomes.
You want to remain hands-on. You’re comfortable testing the product, writing precise requirements, investigating failures, and doing the detailed work required to get an early product right.

Helpful Experience

Enterprise automation, integration platforms, RPA, developer tools, or agent-based products.

new_jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Amazon Customer Service Data Intelligence
new_jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Customer Service Data Intelligence is hiring a Principal Product Manager - Technical to own how we prove that the artificial intelligence serving our customers is safe, correct, and fair.

Customer Service Data Intelligence builds the data and intelligence foundation for Amazon Customer Service. When a customer contacts Amazon, the systems that resolve their issue need context — what they said, what they ordered, what they already tried. Our organization is responsible for turning those interactions into a governed, trustworthy foundation that models and applications can safely consume, and for the privacy and security controls that make consuming it possible at all.

This role exists because of a specific shift. When people handled every interaction, trust was a matter of training and policy. When artificial intelligence handles interactions autonomously, across every channel, trust becomes a matter of architecture. You cannot train an agent into good judgment after the fact, and you cannot audit your way to confidence in a system making decisions continuously. The property has to be engineered in — and increasingly, it has to hold for interactions no person will ever review.

You will own the product charter for that engineering. That means building the capability to verify an automated decision against policy before it executes rather than sampling it afterward, the capability to test our own agents adversarially and continuously rather than waiting for someone to find the gap first, and the capability to show that automated decisions treat customers consistently regardless of the marketplace they contact from, the language they speak, or the channel they use.

The most interesting part of this role is that the problem is genuinely unsolved. There is no vendor to buy this from and no established playbook to copy. You will define what "provably safe" means for customer-facing artificial intelligence at Amazon's scale, then build the products that make it the default path rather than the careful path. You will do it alongside security engineers, applied scientists, and legal partners, and your work will set the standard other teams build against.

Key job responsibilities

Own the product vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap for security and privacy intelligence across Amazon Customer Service artificial intelligence systems
Define requirements for translating customer service policies into machine-verifiable logic, so automated decisions can be checked against policy before they execute rather than sampled afterward
Own the product roadmap for continuous adversarial testing of customer service agents, including pre-launch security posture scoring as a launch requirement
Define and operate a fairness verification and monitoring framework that measures whether automated decisions produce consistent outcomes across customer segments, and escalates when they do not
Map product capabilities to regulatory obligations so compliance evidence is generated as a byproduct of operation rather than assembled on request
Chair the cross-organization governance forum that resolves policy conflicts, approves time-bounded exceptions, and closes the loop from a detected issue to an updated and re-verified policy
Partner with security engineering, applied science, legal, and agent-building teams to turn findings into launch standards other teams build against
Write the documents that drive decisions at director and vice president level, and define the metrics that show whether the safe path is also the fast path

A day in the life

Your week is split between three kinds of work. The first is depth: sitting with applied scientists and security engineers on how a policy becomes a formal constraint, or reading the output of an adversarial test run against one of our agents and deciding whether what it found is a bug in the agent or a gap in the policy. The second is decision-forcing: chairing the governance forum where security, legal, and the agent-building teams bring cases that need a call — restrict this agent, update that policy, accept this risk — and making sure each decision leaves with an owner and a date. The third is writing. This organization runs on documents, and the roadmap you own gets funded, sequenced, and defended in prose.

You will also spend real time on other teams' problems, because the fastest way to make the safe path the default is to make it cheaper than the alternative for the team shipping next month.

About The Team

Customer Service Data Intelligence builds the foundation that everything else in Customer Service depends on: how interaction data is captured, governed, enriched, traced, and safely consumed. Our teams span data and software engineering, applied science, analytics, and the privacy and security work that determines what any of it can be used for.

We are at an unusual moment. Language became computable, which turned two decades of customer conversations from an operational cost into the most valuable behavioral signal Amazon has — provided we can use it safely. That condition is the work. We are a builder-heavy, document-driven organization that would rather solve a problem once, centrally, than watch every team solve it badly on their own.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree
Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
Experience technical product management
Experience owning and leading significant projects from concept to deployment
Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working directly with Engineers on product enhancements
Experience in project management methodologies, business analysis, or process improvement
Experience programming with at least one software programming language, or experience with Machine Learning and Large Language Model fundamentals, including architecture, training/inference lifecycles, and optimization of model execution
Experience within a customer service/contact center environment
- Experience building security, privacy, or compliance products

new_jobs.description:
Description

Help shape how Whole Foods Market merchants plan, forecast, and make decisions, and put AI-powered tools in their hands to do it better. As a Senior Product Manager, you'll own the product strategy for intelligent automation, next-generation forecasting models, and the data foundations that connect them. You'll work at the intersection of AI/ML, merchant experience, and supply chain data to build capabilities that fundamentally change how category managers operate across one of the world's most trusted grocery brands.

Whole Foods Market is known as the number one grocer suppliers want to be in, and our merchants are central to that reputation. Your job is to make them faster, sharper, and more confident in their decisions, whether that's through AI agents that surface insights at the point of decision, forecasting models that replace legacy planning systems, or data integrations that give merchants end-to-end visibility from supplier to shelf. You'll partner closely with engineering, UX research, analytics, and business teams spanning Amazon and WFM to translate complex technical capabilities into tools merchants trust and adopt.

Key job responsibilities

Own the product strategy and roadmap for AI-powered merchant intelligence tools, including adoption strategy, capability governance, and merchant enablement

Lead cross-functional execution of forecasting model migration: defining success criteria, orchestrating data readiness, managing cross-team dependencies, and driving go/no-go decisions

Drive data integration and catalog harmonization initiatives across multiple systems and organizations, resolving complex upstream and downstream dependencies

Define product requirements for new analytical capabilities, including store clustering, category intelligence, and assortment optimization, from problem framing through OP1 commitment

Earn merchant trust through direct engagement: translating technical capabilities into business value, validating solutions in the field, and building feedback loops that inform the roadmap

Navigate a complex stakeholder landscape spanning product, engineering, supply chain, UX, and merchandising organizations across both Amazon and Whole Foods Market

A day in the life

You'll move between strategic planning and hands-on execution in a single day. One hour you're reviewing AI capability adoption trends and refining the product roadmap, the next you're in a cross-functional sync resolving data dependencies with engineering and analytics partners. After lunch, you might walk category managers through a new capability prototype, then pivot to a UX research debrief that reshapes how you think about the planning workflow. You'll regularly translate between technical ML conversations and practical merchant needs. Expect to partner with teams across Amazon and WFM, navigate ambiguity, and drive clarity where there isn't any yet.

About The Team

Our team builds the tools and platforms that Whole Foods Market category managers rely on to plan, price, promote, and merchandise products. Our portfolio spans assortment planning, pricing optimization, promotions planning, and space and merchandising execution, all powered by a shared data foundation and increasingly driven by AI. We're at an inflection point: transitioning from legacy planning systems to intelligent, data-driven capabilities that change how merchants work. We build in close partnership with Amazon's retail, technology, and operations teams. We move fast, operate with high ambiguity, and value PMs who earn trust with both engineers and merchants.

new_jobs.title: Principal Product Manager - Tech, Security Compliance and Engineering
new_jobs.description:
Description

We are looking for a Principal Product Manager Technical to own the direction of a portfolio of security products with company-wide security, risk, and compliance impact, and to own one of those products directly.

You will define how our products come together: where each one begins and ends, which capabilities belong where, and what the single experience looks like for a builder or a security team moving across them. You will also hold the product function for our most widely adopted product, so the portfolio direction stays anchored to a real backlog rather than becoming strategy at a distance.

This role operates where the business opportunity and the product strategy are not yet defined. You will often need to establish what the problem is before proposing what to build. You will influence engineering priorities, partner-team roadmaps, and security strategy across multiple VP organizations, without owning those teams.

Key job responsibilities

Own portfolio direction. Define how the products relate to each other, where capabilities belong, and what we stop doing. Make the calls on whether a new capability extends an existing product or justifies a new one.
Own a flagship product. Hold the product function for one product directly, including the roadmap and the ranked backlog as single prioritizer.
Define strategy where none exists. Establish the problem, the customer, and the multi-year direction in spaces that are ambiguous today, and bring clarity others can execute against.
Influence across organizations. Build the partnerships our products depend on across security, compliance, legal, and builder-tooling teams in other VP organizations, and reach agreement on approach and sequencing without authority.
Set the measurement bar. Define what outcome we are moving and hold the portfolio to it, replacing activity metrics with evidence that security posture improved.
Develop the product function. Raise the bar on product management practice on the team, mentor product and program managers, and participate in hiring.

A day in the life

You will move between horizons. In the same day you may resolve a boundary question between two products, review a specification with a senior engineer, and reset expectations with a partner team whose roadmap ours depends on.

You will spend meaningful time outside our organization, because most of what limits us is a dependency or a relationship we have not built yet. You will write the documents that make ambiguous, contested decisions reviewable by senior leadership, and you will own the outcome of those decisions.

About The Team

We are a team of product managers, program managers, engineers, and security engineers building the products that make security the default rather than a gate. Our portfolio spans three things: preventing issues at the point code is written, assuring that controls are implemented and evidenced, and turning security signals into risk intelligence that tells leaders which risks are worth their attention. Each product has one named owner for what we build and why, and one named owner for delivery, so ownership is unambiguous by design.

Diverse Experiences

Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?

At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture

In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic Qualifications

10+ years of technical product or program management experience
Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
Experience technical product management
Bachelor's degree

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working directly with Engineers on product enhancements
Experience owning a suite of related products or a platform portfolio
Experience with security, risk intelligence, compliance, or governance products
Experience building developer-facing platforms adopted at scale across a large engineering population
Experience with AI-assisted development tooling and agentic workflows
Experience turning regulatory obligations into durable product capability
Experience mentoring product managers and raising the bar on product practice
MBA or equivalent

Description

AWS Elemental Inference is an AI-powered video understanding service that analyzes live and file-based video in real time, producing structured metadata that drives monetization, content transformation, and audience engagement at scale. The service delivers capabilities including intelligent video reframing, real-time highlight detection, automated subtitling, and contextual metadata for advertising workflows. Our customers today include the world's largest broadcasters, streaming platforms, and sports leagues. The core technology, real-time visual understanding at scale, is applicable to any domain where video carries signal that needs to be extracted and acted on.

We are looking for a Principal Product Manager to own the product strategy, roadmap, and commercial success of Elemental Inference. This is a single-threaded owner role. You will define what we build, why we build it, and how we bring it to market. You will work directly with applied scientists training video foundation models, engineers operating a real-time inference service, and customers running production workloads on it.

This role requires someone who can operate at the intersection of AI/ML product development and commercial execution. You will own the P&L, define pricing and packaging strategy, and drive adoption across a portfolio that spans AI inference, video monetization, and content intelligence. You will make trade-off decisions between expanding into new capabilities and verticals versus deepening quality and reducing cost on what exists today. You will represent Elemental Inference to AWS leadership, cross-org partners, and directly to customers.

Key job responsibilities

Own the product strategy, roadmap, and P&L for Elemental Inference. Set pricing, define packaging, monitor revenue, and adjust GTM approach based on adoption data and customer feedback.
Prioritize features based on customer requirements, revenue impact, competitive dynamics, and technical feasibility. Make explicit scope decisions between breadth (new capabilities, new verticals) and depth (quality, latency, cost).
Partner with the applied science team on model roadmap decisions. Translate customer needs into science requirements and define the bar for production readiness.
Drive cross-service integration with adjacent Elemental services (monetization, live encoding, VOD processing) to deliver end-to-end intelligent media workflows.
Lead cross-org initiatives that span multiple AWS organizations, building alignment on joint product development where shared customer problems require coordinated solutions.
Engage directly with strategic enterprise customers to validate product direction, close design partnerships, and drive adoption of launched features.
Define and manage the partner ecosystem strategy for data dependencies (sports data providers, content licensing) that enable product capabilities.
Identify and evaluate expansion opportunities where the core technology creates value in adjacent domains beyond the service's initial market.
Represent Elemental Inference at industry events and with AWS leadership. Communicate product vision, competitive positioning, and business performance with clarity.

About The Team

AWS Elemental provides the most comprehensive portfolio of media services in the cloud, purpose-built to prepare, process, deliver, and monetize video at global scale. We support technology that delivers outstanding viewing experiences to millions of viewers worldwide, from the largest live sporting events to 24/7 linear channels and on-demand libraries. Our customers include the world's leading broadcasters, streaming platforms, and sports leagues.

new_jobs.title: Principal Product Manager - Technical, External Services, AWS, GenAIUX
new_jobs.description:
DESCRIPTION

The AWS CX GenAIUX team is building intelligent, personalized experiences that meet users where they are. We believe that different personas—builders, operators, decision-makers, learners—deserve purpose-built GenAI applications tailored to their workflows, mental models, and goals. We are a fast-moving team that values customer obsession, bias for action, and thinking big. We believe that our customers need not to learn AWS, rather we should learn customer’s and enable them to build on AWS wherever and however they prefer. We follow their intent and help them build.

Our team sits at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence and User Experience — Our vision is to cater to the need of every personality of the customers, define the future of persona driven applications and democratizing innovation for all customers on earth. We believe that different personas — builders, operators, decision-makers, and learners — deserve purpose-built GenAI applications tailored to their workflows, mental models, and goals. We measure success trust earned, adoption of applications and enhancing the AWS adoption.

We're building the future of how people and AI work together on cloud infrastructure, and this role is central to that vision.

About The Role

Model a "builder PM" culture where hands-on experimentation is the norm, not the exception.

We are seeking a Principal Product Manager - Technical to define the ever-evolving persona strategy for AWS's GenAI-powered customer applications, establish the application frameworks that translate persona insights into a portfolio of applications, and drive flywheel for success of our customers at AWS.

This requires a person who can drive a vision with conviction, remain stub-born on the vision yet flexible on the journey. This is a usability problem as much as a technology problem. The challenge is envisioning product for differentiated experiences where each customer intuitively understands the GenAI applications to leverage, trusts them enough to integrate into their life, delegate progressively complex work, and feels in control throughout. You will define how different customer personas experience trust, autonomy, and transparency differently — and translate that into distinct product experiences.

organization-level alignment on what we build, for whom, and why.

This is not a "strategy-only" role. In the era of Generative AI, the most impactful product leaders are hands-on builders who prototype before they prescribe, validate with working artifacts before writing documents, and earn engineering credibility by building alongside their teams. We expect you to be fluent in the tools and technologies you're shaping — capable of prompting, prototyping, and evaluating GenAI systems firsthand (a hands-on builder).

This is a high-ambiguity, high-impact opportunity to make a difference in AWS customer’s life with technology revolution. The problem space is largely undefined: we do not yet have a systematic understanding of how millions of AWS users (both tech and non-tech), e.g. from junior developers to C-suite executives should experience AI-native workflows differently. You will define the strategy, build the mechanisms, set the direction that an experienced engineering team executes against, and personally validate critical bets through hands-on prototyping. You will operate with significant independence, and influencing leadership, roadmap decisions across AWS CX with laser focus on Customers.

Key job responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Persona Strategy & Frameworks (Org-Level)

Define and own the persona strategy for AWS GenAI experiences — establishing a scalable, data-driven framework that the broader organization uses to segment, prioritize, and serve differentiated customer cohorts
Set the methodology for persona research (qualitative and quantitative), and direct L5/L6 PMs, UX researchers, and data scientists who execute against it
Establish a living persona framework that becomes an organizational asset — referenced in OP1/OP2 planning, used by engineering to make architecture decisions, and adopted by adjacent AWS teams

Portfolio Strategy & Application Definition

Translate persona insights into a portfolio of GenAI application concepts, defining the investment thesis for each: target persona, differentiated value, technical moat, and business model
Own the "working backwards" narrative at the portfolio level — authoring L7-grade PR/FAQs that articulate the 3-year vision and secure L8–L10 sponsorship. Supplement narratives with functional prototypes that make the vision tangible.
Make hard prioritization decisions across competing application investments, using a rigorous framework that balances customer impact, technical feasibility, time-to-value, and strategic positioning

Product Roadmap & Org-Level Alignment

Define success metrics grounded in customer outcomes — adoption by persona, task completion rates, trust signals (autonomy granted over time), friction reduction, and retention — with clear input/output metric trees that teams can decompose and own
Identify and escalate strategic trade-offs to senior leadership with clear recommendations

Cross-Functional & External Leadership

Influence senior leadership (L8–L10) with compelling, data-backed narratives that shape organizational priorities and resource allocation
Drive cross-org partnerships (Console, Documentation, Well-Architected, Training & Certification) to ensure persona insights are leveraged broadly
Represent AWS externally — customer advisory boards, re:Invent sessions, whitepapers, live demos — as the thought leader on persona-driven GenAI experiences
Engage directly with external AWS customers to understand their workflows, observe how they interact with agent experiences across personas, and ensure design decisions are grounded in real behavior
Attract, mentor, and develop PM talent; raise the product management bar across the team. Model a "builder PM" culture where hands-on experimentation is the norm, not the exception.

Basic Qualifications

4+ years of technical experience (software development, ML/AI systems, or other hands-on engineering work)
10+ years of technical product management, program management, or engineering experience, with at least 5 years at a senior/principal level owning portfolio-level strategy
Experience delivering large-scale products where you are responsible for the full product lifecycle, from concept through launch
Experience building complex software systems that have been successfully delivered to customers
Demonstrated experience shipping AI/ML or Generative AI products at scale
Hands-on experience building with GenAI tooling — evidence of personal prototyping, prompt engineering, or building functional demos/POCs (not just writing requirements for others to build)
Proven ability to operate in high-ambiguity environments — defining both the problem and the solution where neither is well-understood
Track record of influencing org-level strategy and driving alignment across multiple teams (engineering, science, design, business)
Experience establishing mechanisms and frameworks adopted beyond your immediate team
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent experience)

Preferred Qualifications

MBA or advanced technical degree (MS/PhD in CS, AI/ML, HCI, or related field)
Understanding of Large Language Models, agentic architectures, agentic solutions, and conversational AI — sufficient to discuss architectural trade-offs independently with tech team
Experience with AI development tooling (e.g., Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, LangChain, agent frameworks, evaluation harnesses)
Experience with UX research methodologies — usability testing, customer journey mapping, behavioral analytics, persona development, ethnographic research, Jobs-to-Be-Done
Track record of external thought leadership (conference talks, published papers, live demos at industry events)
Knowledge of AWS services and the AWS customer ecosystem

WHY "HANDS-ON" MATTERS FOR THIS ROLE

In the GenAI era, the speed of innovation means the gap between "strategy" and "execution" must collapse. AI products are probabilistic — their behavior can only be understood through direct experimentation, not specification documents. A PM who hasn't prompted the model, stress-tested edge cases, or built a working prototype simply cannot make informed prioritization decisions about what to build next.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

7+ years of working as a Technical Product Manager experience
5+ years of technical (software development, network development, IT, other related) experience
Experience delivering large-scale SaaS, PaaS or LaaS products where you are responsible for the full product lifecycle, from concept through GTM (go to market)

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

5+ years of working as a Technical Product Manager experience

Microsoft's gaming portfolio reaches hundreds of millions of players across mobile, console, and PC. We are creating premium, player-first ways to connect brands and advertisers with these experiences while protecting the quality and trust players expect.

We are looking for a Principal Product Manager
to execute our monetization demand strategy across our gaming portfolio, with a focus on XBOX and Activision-Blizzard-King (ABK) titles and surfaces. You will show how advertisers show up in our gaming surfaces, defining the customer value, measurement framework, and execution plan that help Microsoft build durable, brand-safe, performance-oriented monetization while keeping the player experience first.

This is a role for a product leader who is energized by ambiguous spaces, complex marketplace dynamics, and the unique creative and commercial dynamics of gaming. You will partner closely with XBOX, engineering, design, data science, sales, business planning, finance, studio, and other partner teams to identify the right opportunities, validate them with evidence, and ship products that improve advertiser outcomes, gaming surface value, and player trust.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Responsibilities

Define and drive the product strategy for gaming monetization across XBOX and Activision Blizzard King, translating business opportunities into clear player and advertiser problems, product bets, success metrics, and execution plans.
Lead product discovery across players, advertisers, studios, sales teams, and engineering partners to identify high-value monetization opportunities across mobile, console, and PC gaming, and sharpen the why now for each investment.
Develop crisp product requirements, roadmap priorities, launch plans, and tradeoff recommendations that balance advertiser demand, player experience quality, marketplace economics, privacy, policy, and technical feasibility.
Partner with engineering, data science, and design to ship scalable monetization products and measurement capabilities that improve yield, quality, relevance, and advertiser confidence across gaming surfaces.
Use data, experimentation, player and customer feedback, and marketplace signals to evaluate product performance, diagnose issues, and make prioritization decisions.
Help evolve gaming monetization from fragmented, surface-by-surface opportunities into a unified, premium, measurable, and durable product portfolio that scales across titles and platforms.
Model Microsoft culture by bringing curiosity, player and customer obsession, growth mindset, inclusive collaboration, and high accountability to cross-functional product work.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree AND 8+ years experience in product/service/program management or software development
OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years experience driving product strategy, roadmap definition, requirements, and execution for complex software, advertising, marketplace, commerce, media, or platform products.
Experience using data, experimentation, customer research, or business analysis to identify opportunities, make product tradeoffs, and measure outcomes.
Experience partnering with engineering and cross-functional stakeholders to deliver products or features from concept through launch and iteration.
Experience communicating (both written and verbal) with stakeholders at all levels while simplifying ambiguous problems and influencing without direct authority.
Passion for gaming, with hands-on experience building games or gaming products, or a genuine interest in games, gaming platforms, and interactive entertainment.
Experience with mobile monetization, including in-app advertising, in-game commerce, or free-to-play monetization models.
7+ years experience in product management, program management, strategy, business planning, advertising technology, marketplace products, or related roles.
Experience in digital advertising, monetization, inventory quality, campaign management, yield optimization, brand safety, measurement, or media marketplaces.
Demonstrated ability to operate in ambiguous, multi-stakeholder environments and convert early signals into structured product plans and measurable outcomes.
Technical fluency with platform architecture, APIs, data pipelines, experimentation systems, privacy/security considerations, or machine learning-driven product experiences.
Ability to reason across user experience, advertiser value, marketplace economics, partner incentives, and long-term platform strategy.
A growth mindset, high judgment, and passion for building products that create customer value while earning user and partner trust.

AWS Payments and Fraud Prevention is hiring a PMT-ES to define and drive large-scale, cross-company initiatives that shape the future of AWS's payment infrastructure. In this role, you will tackle problem spaces that impact the full breadth of AWS services and drive the next wave of strategic growth for the company. You'll focus on long-term deliverables with the opportunity to deliver projects of broad scale and scope. As a member of the product team working across multiple initiatives, you'll collaborate with a group of product leaders and be expected to help solve problems that span multiple business groups.

You'll learn complex technical systems and their interconnections while building relationships across multiple business leaders. You are an excellent communicator—equally comfortable speaking with junior engineers and senior executives. You thrive in ambiguity and move fluidly from one idea to the next as you drive problems to conclusion and discover new areas with business potential.

Overview

With hundreds of millions of users and tens of thousands of business customers across every industry and region, M365 is a key driver of Microsoft’s leadership in cloud services and the shift toward AI-powered productivity. The M365 core platform is fundamental to the success of Office 365, serving as the foundation for every productivity experience and intelligent service across the Microsoft Cloud. It enables new applications and services from both Microsoft and third parties, including Copilot experiences that are significantly enhancing customer productivity worldwide. Given its scale and critical importance, M365 is a prime target for highly sophisticated and well-resourced threat actors. We are seeking an experienced Senior Product Manager, ideally with a background in security or identity, to lead key security initiatives for the platform and its partners across Microsoft.

This position is based in Redmond, Washington and requires the employee be in the office a minimum of 3 days per week.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Play a key role in detecting, investigating, and mitigating security threats; engage in post-incident reviews for security incidents, drive corrective actions to closure, and work alongside architects to translate lessons learned into durable engineering improvements.

new_jobs.description:
Overview

Every request Microsoft 365 serves depends on the network beneath it — a global fabric spanning every geography Microsoft operates in, serving hundreds of millions of people. As Microsoft 365 grows and its infrastructure continues to move toward an Azure-native footprint, the network has to evolve with it: toward explicit, identity-aware connectivity, stronger regional isolation, and smaller failure domains.We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own network connectivity strategy for the platform. That evolution is where you would start, and the charter continues well past it. You will shape long-term architecture direction with the teams that own and depend on the network.This is an AI-first product management role. AI is changing what the PM role consists of, and that change is accelerating. We expect someone who already works this way, or is eager to, and who brings the team with them.This role requires on-call for the platform. The network sits on the critical path for Microsoft 365, and product management here comes with real operational ownership — including occasional out-of-hours engagement during live incidents.This position is based in Redmond, Washington and requires the employee be in the office a minimum of 3 days per week.Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Responsibilities

Own the strategy for network connectivity and its evolution across the platform, and turn that direction into a roadmap teams can execute.
Drive the move to an explicit, regionalized, policy-enforced connectivity model — including the migration sequencing, exception governance, and dependency burn-down that make it real.
Take on high-impact problems across the charter, including scalability, resiliency, segmentation and isolation, capacity, latency, and platform transitions, and drive them to resolution.
Work problems end-to-end: own the outcome even when every step of the work belongs to someone else.
Model the tradeoffs before committing investment, and apply judgment where the model runs out.
Weigh security, reliability, performance, and cost against each other, and prioritize multi-year platform investments with the teams that fund and build them.
Keep failure domains contained and recovery paths intact.Participate in the on-call rotation — help scope and triage live incidents, and turn what you learn from them into root-cause fixes and roadmap priorities.
Set success metrics, OKRs (Objectives and Key Results), and KPIs (key performance indicators), and shape investment priorities with leadership.
Explain complex tradeoffs to executives in a way that leads to decisions.
Mentor other product managers and move the team toward better, AI-forward ways of working.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree AND 5+ years experience in product management and driving a large-scale infrastructure migration or network transition for large scale distributed systems
OR equivalent experience.

Decision Making - The ability to make decisions in a fast-paced, rapidly changing environment. This includes the ability to define, diagnose, and determine an appropriate resolution, recommendation, or decision while considering alternatives and factors (e.g., resources, costs, tradeoffs).
Influence Others - The ability to garner support for initiatives by gaining the respect of others and inspiring trust and confidence.
Negotiation - The ability to achieve mutually satisfying agreements in negotiations with others by listening to their objectives, acting as the company's representative to effectively communicate the company's objective, and seeking common ground and collaborative solutions.

Preferred Qualifications

Technical depth in networking and large-scale distributed systems — enough to reason with architects about how traffic moves, how the network fails, and what it costs; to hold your own in a live incident; and to explain those tradeoffs clearly to any audience.
Includes cloud networking — virtual networks and peering, software-defined networking, address management, and NAT — and how their limits behave at fleet scale.
Experience driving a large-scale infrastructure migration or network transition on a live, high-availability service — including sequencing, rollback, and dependency burn-down.
Fluency with AI-forward ways of working (agents, automation, evaluation sets), or a demonstrated ability to adopt new tooling quickly.
Working knowledge of Layer-7 routing, reverse proxies, or front-door/CDN-class infrastructure.
Zero-trust and network security fundamentals — segmentation, identity-based authorization, mutual TLS, and policy enforcement.
Experience with Microsoft 365, Exchange, Azure infrastructure, or other large multi-tenant platforms — helpful but not required; the platform specifics can be learned.

Description

Amazon Manufacturing Services (AMS) is seeking a Sr. Product Manager, Tech to own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for the manufacturing execution and automation intelligence stack powering Amazon’s first advanced manufacturing facility — a highly automated, first-of-its-kind operation. This facility integrates industrial robotics, end-to-end manufacturing automation, and digital manufacturing to produce systems for Amazon’s global fulfillment network.

Key job responsibilities

Manufacturing Execution Product Strategy

Own the 2–3 year product roadmap for the manufacturing execution stack — from scheduling UX through operator tools to AI-powered optimization
Define the product vision that connects AI-native scheduling intelligence to the physical shop floor experience
Develop and maintain the execution technology strategy across P0 (manual + semi-automated), P1 (AGV integration, real-time optimization), and P2 (AI-enabled autonomous control)
Write compelling narratives (PR/FAQs, 6-pagers, OP docs) that articulate product strategy and secure investment from leadership

Scheduling & Operator Experience

Serve as the operational product partner to the scheduling engineering team — translating manufacturing floor needs, pain points, and workflows into product requirements
Own the operator-facing scheduling experience: how assignments surface, how disruptions are communicated, how overrides are captured, and how the system explains its decisions to the right audience
Drive the scheduling system’s authority progression (Shadow → Advisory → Co-Pilot → Decision Maker) by defining success criteria, measuring override rates, and building supervisor trust through UX design
Define product requirements for scheduling and explainability tools from the operator/supervisor perspective

Machine Connectivity & IIoT

Own the product vision for machine connectivity — defining how equipment telemetry flows from factory floor to data lake to decision systems
Define integration requirements for manufacturing equipment onboarded at the manufacturing facility (industrial lasers, robotic welding cells, automated coating lines, autonomous mobile robots)
Develop product requirements for digital twin capabilities — real-time equipment state, simulation for what-if analysis, and predictive modeling
Partner with automation engineers to define the machine-to-cloud data contract for each equipment class

AI/ML & Continuous Improvement

Define and execute product strategy for AI-driven manufacturing intelligence: predictive maintenance, automated quality inspection, process parameter optimization, and autonomous cell control
Own requirements for the data platform layer that enables ML — feature stores, event streams, model serving infrastructure
Drive the feedback loop between quality outcomes (first-pass yield, scrap rates) and upstream process adjustments — ensuring the system learns and improves continuously
Define the operator interaction model for AI recommendations — when to alert, when to auto-act, when to require human confirmation

Shop Floor Quality & Compliance

Own the product experience for in-line quality: inspection workflows, non-conformance reporting, root cause analysis tools, and SPC dashboards
Define how quality data flows back to both the scheduling system (for replan triggers) and the enterprise system (for financial variance reporting)
Partner with Quality Engineering to translate ISO 9001:2015 requirements into tool capabilities and audit-ready data records

A day in the life

In the morning, you review overnight production data from our prototyping factory — the scheduling system’s override rate dropped to 7% this week, and you’re preparing the case to promote it from Shadow to Advisory mode. You pull the override-reason breakdown to identify two UX issues driving unnecessary supervisor interventions, then draft requirements for the engineering team.

The laser cutting integration team needs a decision on telemetry frequency — you work through the tradeoffs between data granularity (better for predictive maintenance models) and network cost (lower in batch mode), landing on a tiered approach by signal type.

After lunch, you’re on the prototype factory floor shadowing a powder coating operator through a disruption scenario — a rush order just reshuffled the queue, and you observe how the shop floor app communicates the change. new_jobs.title: Principal Applied Scientist
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Core Search and AI team (Bing) is looking for people who want to build the next generation of search using advanced AI technologies, especially large language models, at scale. We are responsible for the largest machine learning models at Microsoft by volume and take pride in being the first in the world to solve many practical AI at Scale challenges. Our work spans a very large scope of scenarios including delivering high quality search results from a massive document corpus, query and document understanding, retrieval and reranking model for search results optimization, as well as AI search grounding, etc.

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Principal Applied Scientist with solid machine learning expertise and can adopt state-of-art AI technologies to improve the relevance for the next generation of search. 

As a team, we leverage the diverse backgrounds and experiences of passionate engineers, scientists, and program managers to help us realize our goal of making the world smarter and more productive. We believe great products are built by inclusive teams of customer-obsessed individuals who trust each other and work together closely.  We collaborate regularly across the company to find technological breakthroughs from groups like Microsoft Research to infusing AI into the rest of Microsoft products like Office and Azure.

Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more, and we believe that artificial intelligence will play a critical role in accomplishing that mission. The Core Search and AI team is the leading applied machine learning team at Microsoft responsible for delivering the highest-quality search experience to over 500M+ monthly active users around the world in Microsoft’s search engine, Bing and other dependent search engines such as Yahoo, DuckDuckGo, and new startups like Neeva.

Starting January 26, 2026, Microsoft AI (MAI) employees who live within a 50- mile commute of a designated Microsoft office in the U.S. or 25-mile commute of a non-U.S., country-specific location are expected to work from the office at least four days per week. This expectation is subject to local law and may vary by jurisdiction.

Responsibilities

You will lead one or more big initiatives leveraging your expertise across a broad research landscape, including advanced research methodologies and applied techniques. You’ll gain deep knowledge of a service, platform, or domain, and drive product opportunities by sharing emerging industry trends and applied technologies.
You will review business requirements and incorporate research insights to meet strategic goals. You’ll provide directions on the types of data and machine learning model strategies needed to solve complex problems and apply deep subject‑matter expertise to drive measurable business impact.
You will support the onboarding of new team members and help develop academic collaborators into effective contributors within multidisciplinary teams. You’ll identify promising research talent, engage with the academic community, and strengthen Microsoft’s long‑term recruiting pipeline.
You will advance LLM post‑training and alignment techniques by designing, implementing, and evaluating novel methods that improve reasoning quality, safety, controllability, and factual grounding across large‑scale models.
You will drive and develop next‑generation search capabilities by building and optimizing retrieval, ranking, and relevance systems that integrate deeply with LLM‑powered experiences.
You will architect and refine RAG pipelines that enhance retrieval fidelity, reduce hallucinations, and deliver more context‑aware, user‑aligned responses in production environments.
You will translate research into production by running experiments, analyzing results, and collaborating with engineering partners to deploy scalable, reliable model improvements.
You will drive scientific rigor through hypothesis‑driven experimentation, reproducible methodologies, and clear documentation of findings, insights, and model behaviors.
You will drive collaborate across disciplines—including research, engineering, product, and design—to shape long‑term strategy for search, alignment, and retrieval‑augmented systems.
You will contribute to a culture of innovation by sharing learnings, mentoring peers, and participating in internal research discussions, reviews, and technical deep dives.

Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years related experience (e.g., statistics, predictive analytics, research)
OR Master's Degree in Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or related field AND 6+ years related experience (e.g., statistics, predictive analytics, research)
OR Doctorate in Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or related field AND 5+ years related experience (e.g., statistics, predictive analytics, research)
OR equivalent experience.

OR Doctorate in Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years related experience (e.g., statistics, predictive analytics, research)
OR equivalent experience.

6+ years of experience coding in Python, C++, C#, C or Java.
6+ year of industry experience applying Machine Learning techniques.
Experience building and improving large scale Machine Learning system for search, ads, and recommendation, adopting LLM.
Research background on Machine Learning, LLM and NLP.
Proficient problem solver: ability to identify and solve problems that the world has not solved before.

new_jobs.description:
The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we’re behind some of Spotify’s most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you’ll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.

Spotify Search handles billions of queries across every market, language, and content type — music, podcasts, audiobooks, videos, playlists, and more. We’re looking for a Principal Product Manager to lead the Search Personalization within our Conversation Product Area, setting the product strategy for how hundreds of millions of users find and discover content on Spotify. This is a leadership role at the intersection of search systems, AI, and user experience. You’ll own the end-to-end strategy for search results — from ranking and relevance to AI-powered features like semantic search, LLM reranking, and AI Overviews — while leading two key Search squads (results ranking and query suggestions). Search is the front door to Spotify; this role shapes what people find when they walk through it.

What You'll Do

Set the product strategy and multi-cycle roadmap for Search Personalization at Spotify — spanning ranking, relevance, retrieval, AI-native features, quality, and trust.
Drive the evolution of Search toward AI-native experiences — AI Overviews, semantic search, LLM reranking — balancing innovation velocity with quality and cost discipline.
Own the Search quality bar: define how relevance, trust, compliance, and user experience connect into a holistic quality framework with measurable outcomes.
Manage Search’s role as a shared surface across many company strategies — build prioritization frameworks, communicate trade-offs, and represent Search at executive forums.
Influence and coach junior PMs working in Search.
Partner with engineering leadership to make architectural decisions that balance short-term delivery with long-term Search infrastructure health.
Drive cross-functional alignment where Search intersects.

Who You Are

You have 8+ years of product management experience, with 3+ years leading search, discovery, or information retrieval products at scale (100M+ users).
You have a deep technical understanding of search systems — ranking architectures, retrieval strategies, evaluation methodology, and the trade-offs between relevance, latency, cost, and freshness.
You have experience with AI/ML-powered search features — semantic search, LLM-based reranking, recommendations, or similar — and can lead a team through the transition from traditional to AI-native search.
You have a track record of managing complex stakeholder landscapes with competing priorities and limited resources, and can build frameworks for principled prioritization.
You think strategically at the portfolio level — you can synthesize across many concurrent initiatives, set a coherent vision, and communicate it clearly to executives.
You communicate with clarity and conviction, with the ability to translate technical complexity into compelling narratives for leadership, bet owners, and cross-functional partners.
You have experience mentoring and developing early-career PMs, and can influence without authority or direct reporting lines.
You bring familiarity with music, audio, or media technology and understand the unique dynamics of content-rich platforms.
You have experience operating Search as a platform that serves multiple internal teams or content verticals.
You have worked in content integrity, trust & safety, or regulatory compliance in the context of search or discovery systems.

Where You'll Be

This role is based in London or Stockholm.
We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.

new_jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Technical (External Services), Region Services
new_jobs.description:
Description

Applicants must be Australian citizens and hold or be eligible to obtain an Australian Government Security Clearance with the ability to successfully complete an Organisational Suitability Assessment. More information regarding security clearances can be found at https://www.agsva.gov.au/.

Based in Melbourne, Sydney or Canberra, we offer relocation support for candidates moving from other states.

The Mission - Why This Program, Why Now?

You're joining at the defining moment of one of the most significant technology programmes Australia has ever undertaken. This programme will build and operate the dedicated cloud giving Australia's national security community and its allies the capability to see more, share more, innovate and act faster than ever before.

The architectural decisions being made now - how we structure services, implement security controls, and automate at scale - will shape how Australia's national security community operates for the next decade. You won't be inheriting someone else's design choices. You'll be making them.

Your Opportunity

Imagine standing at the intersection of strategy, technology, and national purpose, where every product decision you make shapes how an entire AWS cloud region serves Australia's most critical missions. As a Senior Product Manager – Technical, External Services (PMT-ES), you won't just manage a product backlog. You'll own the end-to-end lifecycle of externally-facing AWS services. From defining the technical vision and product strategy, through architecture and launch, to driving adoption and operational excellence with the engineering and IT leaders who depend on your services every day.

This is a role for someone who thrives on complexity, brings deep full-stack technical fluency, and craves impact at scale. You'll define technical requirements alongside engineering teams building the next generation of cloud infrastructure, evaluate architecture trade-offs across performance, scalability, and security, and serve as the voice of the customer for external engineers and IT professionals integrating AWS services into their most critical workloads. When a customer escalation hits, you'll own it, diving deep with engineering to understand the problem, resolve it, and communicate clearly back to technically sophisticated customers.

The Region Services team is redefining how AWS designs, builds, and operates regions. You'll engage directly with technical decision-makers at Australia's most important organisations, understanding how they architect their solutions, generalising requirements across diverse customer personas, and driving service awareness, adoption, and evolution. Your work will directly accelerate Australia's cloud capability and set the standard for how sovereign cloud regions evolve worldwide.

If you're energised by working at the deepest technical levels of cloud services, engaging directly with the engineers and architects who build on AWS, and delivering products that genuinely change how nations operate in the cloud, this is your moment.

Key job responsibilities

Own the end-to-end product lifecycle for externally-facing AWS services in the region, defining service vision, strategy, technical requirements, and roadmaps, while driving capacity planning and service performance.
Define and prioritise product roadmaps by engaging directly with external technical customers (engineers, architects, IT professionals), analysing usage data, service performance metrics, and competitive dynamics to anticipate where customers need to go next.
Partner deeply with engineering teams on architecture decisions, evaluating proposals across performance, scalability, latency, and security trade-offs. Define detailed technical requirements and hold engineering to high standards for service quality.
Serve as the Voice of the Customer distilling requirements from diverse sets of technical customers, understanding how the service integrates into their architectures, and generalising needs across customer personas to define the right product direction.
Own service adoption and operational excellence driving awareness, adoption, and performance optimisation with customers. Own customer escalations, and service communications until issues are resolved.
Collaborate across engineering, design, finance, sales, legal, and operations to align stakeholders, make smart trade-offs, and deliver outcomes that balance customer value with business sustainability.

A day in the life

Your morning begins with a review of service readiness dashboards, tracking which services are on track for launch, where integration testing is surfacing issues, and which customer workload requirements are driving prioritisation decisions. You spot a gap between a customer's architecture needs and a service's planned launch configuration, and pull together the data to make the case for adjusting the rollout sequence.

By mid-morning, you're in a technical design review with the engineering team. A service needs to meet specific compliance requirements before it can go live so you're evaluating the architecture against these constraints, defining the technical requirements, and working through trade-offs between launch timeline and operational readiness.

After lunch, you join a working session with a customer's cloud architects who are planning to migrate mission-critical workloads into the region. They need to understand which services will be available at launch, how they'll perform at scale, and what their migration path looks like. You walk through the region's service roadmap, capture their architectural requirements, and feed those directly into your prioritisation decisions.

The afternoon shifts to a cross-functional alignment session. You're bringing together engineering, capacity planning, compliance, and business development to resolve competing priorities for the launch window. You present your readiness assessment backed by customer commitment data and technical dependency analysis, and drive the group to a decision on what ships in the initial launch versus the fast-follow roadmap.

You end the day knowing that the region you're building will directly enable Australia's national security community to operate with confidence in the cloud and that tomorrow will bring an entirely new set of technical challenges worthy of your expertise.

About The Team

The Region Services team redefines the way AWS designs, builds, and operates AWS regions to enable new cloud infrastructure and services offerings to customers across every industry and of every size, including startups, enterprises, and public sector organisations.

Amazon values inclusive experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. Description

At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. Serving over 200M customers globally, our Customer Service (CS) organization is at the forefront of shaping how customers experience Amazon. Our team enables Amazon CS’ frontline teams to deliver seamless, consistent, convenient, and delightful customer service to all our customers (including our consumers, businesses, and drivers) across every interaction.

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to serve as the Service Delivery organization’s single threaded leader for associate-facing products. This role is responsible for owning the associate empowerment charter to support associate-facing product roadmaps and strategy across multiple Tech teams. An ideal candidate will combine product management depth in customer service operations with a demonstrated ability to implement AI-driven automation and modern project management tooling across distributed teams.

You will partner with Tech teams to define and design the end-to-end experience of associate and frontline leader-facing tools, including AC3 and Inspire. You will evaluate and improve existing tooling and create new tech and AI driven solutions, consistently enhancing associate experiences and empowering our teams. You will work backward from associate pain points, design products, define product requirements, and partner with engineering, operations, and stakeholder teams to deliver solutions at scale. You will balance short-term tactical improvements with long-term strategic bets to continuously raise the bar on the associate experience.

The ideal candidate combines strong product and program management capabilities, business acumen in operations and deep associate empathy. You are equally comfortable diving into data and anecdotes to identify opportunities, writing PRFAQs, vision docs and BRDs, and influencing without authority to align cross-functional teams on a shared vision. You thrive in ambiguity, are biased toward action, and have a track record of delivering products that meet their customers’ needs. Disrupting the status quo by challenging mental models, organizational focus, and technology will be part of your day to day.

This role can be located in Hyderabad.

Own the end-to-end product strategy and associate empowerment products charter for Service Delivery, including associate and frontline leadership facing products
Lead strategic planning processes, working with leaders across the organization to set goals, define priorities, and allocate resources.

Translate associate and frontline leadership insights, data signals, and business requirements into actionable product improvements and scalable solutions.
Partner with Tech, UX design, data science, and operations teams to deliver product features from concept through launch and iteration. Create frameworks to help Tech stakeholders raise the bar on the associate experience.
Influence and align senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders on product direction through compelling narratives and data-driven recommendations
Apply analytical rigor to frame trade-offs and enable leaders to make well-informed decisions.

Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition

Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product

Preferred Qualifications

Experience relying on analytics and data to cultivate deep customer empathy, shape product decisions and track effectiveness of change
Experience working with a cross-functional team across design, operations, and engineering team to meet high-reaching goals

Description

This role is part of the IES Shopping team and owns the mission of helping every emerging shopper instantly discover, understand, and act on the best value available to them — surfacing personalized savings across the shopping funnel from Home page to Cart — driving purchase confidence and conversion across emerging markets worldwide.

Emerging shoppers are highly price-sensitive and compare offers across retailers — yet face a fragmented value landscape: savings are scattered across different promotion types with no unified view of their true net effective price. Shoppers miss applicable savings, struggle to compare cost-to-own, and abandon purchases because the "best price" is unclear. This role exists to unify that value narrative at scale — combining all savings instruments into a single, transparent, personalized view and ensuring every shopper can maximize savings and make every purchase feel affordable.

Define and drive the long-term Value CX vision and roadmap — Own the multi-year strategy for savings discovery and value communication across emerging markets. Translate business strategy and voice of shopper into a prioritized, logically sequenced product roadmap. Create buy-in with senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
Own execution from requirements through launch — Partner with UX and engineering to develop high-quality requirements, manage scope, and deliver key capabilities on time. Create and execute go-to-market plans, drive adoption, and continually optimize based on performance metrics.
Partner across business and technology teams — Influence Payments, Affordability, Marketing, and global platform teams to integrate savings instruments into a unified value experience. Drive prioritization of emerging-market requirements in global partner roadmaps.
Operate with strategic range — Be equally comfortable generating a 3-year vision and executing hands-on, day-to-day problem solving with quick, effective action plans. Prepare and present business reviews to senior management.
